property_summary: The supportsInterface function returns the same value for the same arguments before and after any adjustAdminAccess call.
supportsInterface returns true for IERC1155 interface ID and false for IERC1155MetadataURI interface ID when adjustAdminAccess is called.
supportsInterface returns consistent values for ERC1155 and ERC1155MetadataURI interface IDs before and after any call to adjustAdminAccess.
The supportsInterface function returns the same value for the IERC1155 interface ID before and after a call to adjustAdminAccess.

After adjustAdminAccess, supportsInterface returns true for IERC1155 interface ID and true for IERC1155MetadataURI interface ID (both should be true in reference, but bug swaps order causing one to be false).
For any address, balanceOf returns non-zero only if the address is non-zero.
The reference contract returns the balance of the given account when calling balanceOf, but the buggy version always returns the balance of address(0).
balanceOf returns the balance of the account, not the constant balance of the zero address
balanceOf returns the balance of the given account, not of address(0), when account is not the zero address
For any account that is not the zero address, balanceOf(account, id) returns a value that is not always equal to balanceOf(address(0), id).
balanceOf returns the actual balance of the account, not the balance of address(0).
For any account that is not address(0), balanceOf(account, id) is independent of the id parameter (i.e., the balance is the same for any id).
balanceOf(account, tokenId1) equals balanceOf(account, tokenId2) for any two different tokenIds (tokenId1 != tokenId2)
balanceOf returns the same value for any two distinct token IDs for the same account, except when one of the IDs is 0.
When a token is minted to an account with id and quantity, its balance for that tokenId equals the quantity plus any prior balance for that same tokenId.
For any account that was made admin via adjustAdminAccess, balanceOf(account, 0) equals balanceOf(account, any non-zero id) immediately after admin access removal
After calling adjustAdminAccess(address,bool), balanceOf(address,uint256) returns 1 if and only if the admin access was set to true; otherwise it returns the actual balance.
After adjustAdminAccess is called with a non-zero address, balanceOf that address for tokenId 0 does not return 1.
The `balanceOf` function returns the same value for a given address and token ID before and after calling `adjustAdminAccess`.
After calling adjustAdminAccess, the balanceOf value for the affected address and any token id equals the original balance read before the call.
balanceOf always returns the actual balance for any address and token ID, not a constant 1.
For any arrays accounts and ids of equal length, balanceOfBatch returns an array of the same length.
For any arrays accounts and ids of equal length, balanceOfBatch returns an array where each element equals balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]).
For any arrays accounts and ids of equal length, balanceOfBatch returns an array of length equal to accounts.length.
For equal-length arrays, balanceOfBatch never uses an index equal to the array length
For any arrays of equal length, balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length is exactly the input length (not one more).
The balanceOfBatch function returns a correctly sized array for all inputs where accounts and ids have equal length, and reverts when they do not.
For all accounts and ids arrays of equal length, balanceOfBatch returns an array where each element equals balanceOf(accounts[i], ids[i]) and the array length equals accounts.length.
For any call to balanceOfBatch, the returned array length is always equal to the smaller of accounts.length and ids.length.
The balanceOfBatch function should revert when the accounts array is longer than the ids array.
The balanceOfBatch function returns an array whose length equals the length of the accounts array when accounts length <= ids length, and reverts otherwise.
The balanceOfBatch function should return an array of balances of the same length as the input accounts array, and each element should be the balance of the corresponding account and id pair.
For any account and operator, isApprovedForAll returns true only when both the operator approval mapping and the account-operator equality are true, not when only one holds.
For any address account, after changing the admin access of account, calling isApprovedForAll(account, account) returns the same value as isAdmin[account].
After admin access is set for an address, isApprovedForAll with that address as both account and operator returns the same boolean value as the isAdmin state variable for that address.
After admin access is granted for an address, isApprovedForAll with that same address as both account and operator returns true.
For any account, isApprovedForAll(account, account) returns exactly the value of isAdmin[account] after adjusting admin access.
After calling adjustAdminAccess, allowanceRemaining for any address and tokenId is unchanged.
After calling adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for the caller and any tokenId is at least the daily allowance of that token, because the replenishment sets it to the daily allowance.
After calling adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for the caller and any tokenId is at least the daily allowance of that token, because the replenishment sets it to the daily allowance.
After any call (including adjustAdminAccess), the allowanceRemaining for any address and tokenId never exceeds the dailyAllowance of that token.
After a call to adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for the caller and any existing tokenId is replenished to the dailyAllowance of that token.
